f: He impressed John Lennon by playing the lead guitar part of “Raunchy” on the upper deck of a Liverpool bus.
On the group's first tour of Scotland in 1960 he called himself “Carl Harrison”, after Carl Perkins.
He co-founded HandMade Films in 1978, initially to make Monty Python's Life of Brian.

3lmR0qMiGuoIF9UC54egcG.name: Aldous Harding
f: She was born Hannah Sian Topp in 1990.
She made her recording debut at 13, singing with her mother on “Exactly What to Say”, a song they wrote together.
“The Barrel”, from her third album Designer, won the 2019 APRA Silver Scroll award.

4fFSyYQa0jRwFSunVahGw8.name: TTRRUUCES
f: They are a group from London.

0jOs0wnXCu1bGGP7kh5uIu.name: Tim Maia
f: In Tijuca he taught guitar to other children, including his friends Erasmo Esteves and Roberto Carlos.
With Jorge Ben, he pioneered samba rock and samba funk.
His first LP, Tim Maia (1970), topped the charts in Rio de Janeiro for 24 weeks.

5mFKYdmiYwNJTDtSzgFyQx.name: Andy Shauf
f: He is also lead singer of the indie rock band Foxwarren.
He played almost every instrument on his 2016 album The Party himself; only the strings were by Colin Nealis.
He was a drummer in the pop punk band Captain until 2006.

64RBScSzzcUegqlm1nqZgK.name: Johnny Parry
f: The Johnny Parry Trio and Chamber Orchestra started in 2002.

0fA0VVWsXO9YnASrzqfmYu.name: Kid Cudi
f: He first got noticed with “Day ‘n’ Nite”, which he self-published on his MySpace page before it became an online hit.
He left Cleveland in 2005 with $500 and a demo tape and moved in with his uncle, jazz drummer Kalil Madi, in the South Bronx.
In 2006 he ran into his future mentor Kanye West in a Virgin Megastore.

0dU2EKM6vca3xmJ9kl8zoI.name: Blue Sky Black Death
f: The duo's name is “a skydiving phrase alluding to beauty and death”.
They were Ryan Maguire, known as Kingston, and Ian Taggart, known as Young God and later Televangel.
Their project with Ceschi, Deadpan Darling, went unreleased when most of its final mixes were lost on a crashed hard drive; its recovery was announced in 2021.

27DCwiPx5ocQsf4K43SlIL.name: Colin Blunstone
f: First recruited as a rhythm guitarist, he turned up to his first rehearsal with two black eyes from playing rugby.
In 1969 he released three singles under the pseudonym Neil MacArthur, including a remake of “She's Not There”.
He sang on four Alan Parsons Project albums between 1978 and 1985.

60nDKjd690Luygtd3Fm0Cu.name: Ogi
f: Ogi is a Nigerian-American singer, songwriter and multi-instrumentalist.

6XiSck3QPuXk7ho6zlDz3P.name: The Bees
f: They come from Ventnor on the Isle of Wight and are known in the United States as A Band of Bees.
Their 2002 record Sunshine Hit Me was nominated for the Mercury Prize.
Their cover of “A Minha Menina”, an Os Mutantes track originally by Jorge Ben, was used in a Citroën car advert.

5CzlICF8GCY0pRC82MKrhX.name: Labi Siffre
f: He appears as a violin player in the video for Madness's 1981 cover of his “It Must Be Love”, which reached No. 4 in the UK.
After leaving school he worked as a taxi driver and a deliveryman before concentrating on music.
In 1978 he tried to represent the UK at Eurovision with “Solid Love”, which placed fifth of 12 songs in A Song for Europe.

6PBv8t9YTLggA9ZMwpeoqj.name: Joan As Police Woman
f: Joan As Police Woman comes from Biddeford in the United States.

42WJFNdxsAgcn9PfjT61Z3.name: Eleanor Friedberger
f: She is one half of the indie rock duo The Fiery Furnaces, with her older brother Matthew.
She filmed the video for “In Between Stars” herself, with help from former Sonic Youth frontwoman Kim Gordon.
All four of her solo albums, from Last Summer (2011) to Rebound (2018), reached the top 20 of the Billboard Heatseekers Albums chart.

6LWofoi18999gZK0EgVSjv.name: Tess Henley
f: In 2014 producer Don Was picked her as Guitar Center Singer-Songwriter III grand prize winner, the competition's first female winner.
She started Suzuki Method piano lessons at the age of three.
In December 2020 she featured on “Funny Seeing You Here” from Jack Harlow's album Thats What They All Say.

23EA28263XvtIrXuySX6oI.name: Francis and the Lights
f: “And the Lights” refers both to the lights on a stage and to the pixels on a computer screen.
Its founder drove across the US in a decommissioned postal truck to New York City, where he formed Francis and the Lights.
In November 2008 Starlite set the band up as a limited liability company instead of signing a record deal.

2kTZfKGZEj8R76z3ooKOF1.name: Your Smith
f: Born Caroline Smith, she fronted the indie folk band Caroline Smith and the Good Night Sleeps and has performed as Your Smith since 2018.
At 16 she was playing Zorbaz Pizza restaurants in Detroit Lakes and opened for B. B. King in Duluth and Rochester.
In 2014 she released a single with Lizzo called “Let 'em Say”.

7nwUJBm0HE4ZxD3f5cy5ok.name: Aretha Franklin
f: Her first single, “Never Grow Old”, came out on J.V.B. Records in 1956.
She won the first eight Grammy Awards given for Best Female R&B Vocal Performance, from 1968 to 1975.
In 1987 she became the first female artist inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

2AV6XDIs32ofIJhkkDevjm.name: Curtis Mayfield
f: He got his first guitar at ten and later recalled loving it so much he used to sleep with it.
He wrote “People Get Ready” for the Impressions in 1965; Rolling Stone ranked it No. 24 among the 500 Greatest Songs of All Time in 2004.
He founded his own label, Curtom Records, in Chicago in 1968.

5QdyldG4Fl4TPiOIeMNpBZ.name: Big Thief
f: Adrianne Lenker and Buck Meek met at a show in Boston and began performing as a duo after meeting again in Brooklyn.
Drummer James Krivchenia first joined as the band's sound engineer.
All four members attended the Berklee College of Music in Boston.

1Pag7p4HbSdZIDzgNLsk39.name: Fanny
f: The band was founded by sisters June and Jean Millington, who had played together since moving from the Philippines to California in the early 1960s.
They played on Barbra Streisand's 1971 albums Stoney End and Barbra Joan Streisand, as she wanted to record with a small band.
David Bowie wrote to them admiring their work and showed them mime techniques at a post-show party.

3RyJG8xp58XSmsiuIySzUj.name: Adam Green
f: His Moldy Peaches duet “Anyone Else But You” was featured in the film Juno.
Until Jacket Full of Danger in 2006, all his albums had been released on the 22nd of the month.
His first film, The Wrong Ferarri, released in April 2011, was shot entirely on iPhone.

5ROABVYKJnEJa7ilOwceaq.name: Binki Shapiro
f: Binki Shapiro comes from Los Angeles.

2rc78XDH9zuJP6bm78lU8Z.name: Derek & The Dominos
f: The recording of George Harrison's album All Things Must Pass marked their formation, and Harrison took part in their first session as a band.
Their first gig was a charity concert at London's Lyceum Theatre on 14 June 1970.
Clapton recalls that Ashton suggested “Del and the Dominos”, having taken to calling the guitarist “Derek” or “Del” since the Delaney & Bonnie tour.

3DiDSECUqqY1AuBP8qtaIa.name: Alicia Keys
f: A classically trained pianist, she began composing at 12 and was signed by Columbia Records at 15.
Her 2005 live album Unplugged made her the first female artist to have an MTV Unplugged project debut at number one on the Billboard 200.
In 2023 she wrote her first Broadway musical, Hell's Kitchen, which won two Tony Awards.

55LHFEtIplWhsfyWZUwkf4.name: Foxygen
f: Rado and France started the band in high school when both were 14, and their early music won first place in Agoura High School's Battle of the Bands.
In early 2011 producer Richard Swift ‘discovered’ them after they handed him one of their EPs at a Mynabirds show in New York.

5gl6pfPwJ1coivVUMZPiS9.name: Dennis Wilson
f: He was the group's drummer and its only dedicated surfer.
Brian wrote the band's debut record, “Surfin'”, at Dennis's urging.
He co-starred in the 1971 film Two-Lane Blacktop, his only acting role.

1bdAJUX6JPsnYHbTl5jbk6.name: Joan Armatrading
f: She taught herself guitar on a £3 instrument bought from a pawn shop in exchange for two prams.
In 1968 she joined a touring production of the musical Hair, where she met lyricist Pam Nestor in 1970.
She wrote and performed “Flight of the Wild Geese”, which was used over the opening and end titles of the 1978 war film The Wild Geese.

2GVyv9OLNp6cmxfUDbGrXM.name: Jack Nitzsche
f: As arranger and conductor for Phil Spector, he orchestrated the Wall of Sound on almost all of Spector's hits.
He co-wrote “Needles and Pins” for Jackie DeShannon; it was later recorded by the Searchers.
In 1983 he won the Academy Award for Best Original Song for co-writing “Up Where We Belong”.

6s92YZUPkTK1HL1WIGrPKE.name: Patrick Wolf
f: His writing and recordings caught the attention of Fat Cat Records, which gave him an Atari computer and a mixing console.
He has made guest appearances on viola with Arcade Fire, Owen Pallett, CocoRosie and The Hidden Cameras.
In December 2008 he told NME of his plan to sell £10 shares in an album through bandstocks.com.

6SOQFIN80ymdMZAg8LmQ3n.name: Gwyneth Herbert
f: As the duo Black Coffee, Herbert and Rutter won a Polish television music competition judged by a former member of Boney M.
Blue Note picked up her 2006 album Between Me and the Wardrobe, recorded in three days, making her the label's first UK signing in 30 years.
In 2008 a joint project of Peter Gabriel and Bowers & Wilkins commissioned her to record an acoustic album at Gabriel's Real World Studios.

3ceQN2NVlLg1hgTzljDE4n.name: Half Moon Run
f: Devon Portielje joined after answering a Craigslist ad for a bassist or drummer, despite being neither.
Their song “Full Circle” was used in a 2013 trailer for Ubisoft's Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag.
Their third album, A Blemish in the Great Light, won Adult Alternative Album of the Year at the 2020 Juno Awards.

4Bb8rhvCjLOjNOl1DbFkph.name: Loney dear
f: Emil Svanängen self-released his first album, The Year of River Fontana, in 2003, recorded in a basement in Jönköping and issued on home-made CD-Rs.
He appears on “This Boy” from I'm From Barcelona's 2006 album Let Me Introduce My Friends.
In 2017 he signed to Peter Gabriel's Real World Records.

3nFkdlSjzX9mRTtwJOzDYB.name: JAŸ-Z
f: Known as “Jazzy” in his neighbourhood, he took the stage name Jay-Z in homage to his mentor Jaz-O.
With no major-label deal, he sold burned CDs out of his car and set up Roc-A-Fella Records with Damon Dash and Kareem Burke.
He was the first rapper to be inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame.

5K4W6rqBFWDnAN6FQUkS6x.name: Kanye West
f: His first official production credits came at 19, on eight tracks of Chicago rapper Grav's 1996 album Down to Earth.
He was a producer for Jay-Z's Roc-A-Fella Records, known for a “chipmunk soul” style, before the label signed him as a recording artist.

4wo1267SJuUfHgasdlfNfc.name: The Raconteurs
f: The band grew from Jack White and Brendan Benson writing “Steady, As She Goes” together in an attic one hot summer.
Lawrence and Keeler were originally in the Greenhornes, while White and Lawrence went on to join the Dead Weather.
In Australia they are called The Saboteurs, because a Queensland band was already using the name Raconteurs.

3ZXXJ9nO1Dn9B0AJ25eAQY.name: Hamilton Leithauser
f: He is the lead singer of the Walkmen, with whom he made seven studio albums between 2000 and 2014.
As a teenager he had a summer job at Inner Ear Studios in Arlington, Virginia, where he helped engineer Fugazi's Red Medicine.
His 2020 live album, Live! at Café Carlyle, collects 10 recordings made during his residency at New York's Café Carlyle.

7MhMgCo0Bl0Kukl93PZbYS.name: Blur
f: Blur formed in December 1988 when Alex James joined Damon Albarn's band Circus, which then changed its name to Seymour, after J. D. Salinger's Seymour: An Introduction.
They played their first gig in summer 1989 in the goods shed of the East Anglian Railway Museum at Chappel & Wakes Colne.
Food Records disliked the band's original name, so the group picked Blur from a list of alternatives the label drew up.

3hyGGjxu73JuzBa757H6R5.name: The Mountain Goats
f: The name is a reference to the Screamin' Jay Hawkins song “Yellow Coat”.
For many years Darnielle was its only member, despite the plural name.
Through the 1990s they were known for lo-fi home recordings, most notably made on a cassette-deck boombox.

3mY9Ii0cL5SQxpOTAm8SHx.name: Warren Zevon
f: By 13 he was an occasional visitor to Igor Stravinsky's home, where he briefly studied modern classical music alongside Robert Craft.
In the early 1970s he toured with the Everly Brothers as keyboard player, band leader and musical coordinator.
While playing at the Dubliner Bar in Sitges, near Barcelona, he wrote “Roland the Headless Thompson Gunner” with the bar's owner, David Lindell.

3wrtQM9ICPPeHwoc1GWiyV.name: Teleman
f: Pete Cattermoul and brothers Jonny and Thomas Sanders were previously in the indie band Pete and the Pirates.
The name was inspired by an album by the composer Georg Philipp Telemann that they found in a charity shop.
Bernard Butler produced their debut album, Breakfast, released in mid-2014.

3DL71JYSG6VREkmLSzfWhU.name: Efterklang
f: The name comes from the Danish word for “remembrance” or “reverberation”.
In September 2008 they performed Parades in full with the Danish National Chamber Orchestra at the Copenhagen Concert Hall.
In 2012 they toured their fourth album, Piramida, with an orchestra and Budgie of Siouxsie and the Banshees as guest drummer.

1i8jM74ElAevHmCU1sbNJM.name: Dean & Britta
f: Dean Wareham and Britta Phillips were both in Luna, which Wareham formed in 1991 after leaving Galaxie 500.
Their first album started as a Wareham solo project until he heard Phillips' demos and asked her to join.
Peter Kember, aka Sonic Boom, made a remix mini-LP of L'Avventura called Sonic Souvenirs.

6v0kvTi9pOI2ZFrWGQhdsc.name: Apollo 100
f: Parker formed Apollo 100 in late 1971 with fellow session musicians including drummer Clem Cattini and guitarist Vic Flick.
None of their records after “Joy” was as successful, and they broke up in 1973.

7pZFNZpqGlLKcQcN0GCmdP.name: Tom Parker
f: He arranged the US Top 20 hit “Chirpy Chirpy Cheep Cheep” and a number of Don Fardon's recordings.
He worked with groups including The Mark Leeman 5, Jimmy James and the Vagabonds, and Eric Burdon with the New Animals.
He went on to form the New London Chorale.

6CD0HbcaKmuVB3NHJJgSdH.name: Deep Sea Diver
f: They self-released their first album, History Speaks, on their own label, High Beam Records, in 2012.
In July 2023 they were announced as support for fellow Seattle band Pearl Jam on several dates of its autumn 2023 North American tour.
They signed with Sub Pop in September 2024.

2wJ4vsxWd7df7dRU4KcoDe.name: Sharon Van Etten
f: She played Rachel in both series of the Netflix drama The OA.
The National's Aaron Dessner produced her 2012 album Tramp, recorded in his home studio in Brooklyn.
She wrote the score for the 2016 film Strange Weather in a practice space she shared with Michael Cera.

0OnPrsDBROxkpC3qbFnL6L.name: FFS
f: The name is an abbreviation of Franz Ferdinand and Sparks, the two bands that formed the group.
The two bands first worked on music together in 2004, after discovering they were fans of each other.
Ron and Russell Mael of Sparks came across Alex Kapranos while he was looking for a dentist in San Francisco.
Allen decided to move to Los Angeles in 1977 after fellow Tulsa natives Phil Seymour and Dwight Twilley met with success.
Mike Gallo had already come up with the idea and name for the band after spending time in the UK.
As a three-piece they signed with Greg Shaw's Bomp! Records in 1978 to record a single.

3zunDAtRDg7kflREzWAhxl.name: Eels
f: The name was chosen so the band's records would sit next to E's solo albums, but Eagles and Earth, Wind and Fire releases ended up in between.
They won Best International Breakthrough Act at the 1998 BRIT Awards.
Their song “My Beloved Monster” is on the soundtrack of Shrek.

6XtG9W2KkPiQ6n1rlIvTJE.name: Robert Ellis
f: He started out performing as “Eyes Like Lions” in 2005 in his hometown of Lake Jackson, Texas.
American Songwriter magazine named his second album, Photographs, one of the top 50 albums of 2011.
He has toured with Alabama Shakes, Old Crow Medicine Show and the Old 97's.

7guDJrEfX3qb6FEbdPA5qi.name: Stevie Wonder
f: At 11 he sang his own song “Lonely Boy” to Ronnie White of the Miracles, who took him to audition at Motown, where Berry Gordy signed him.
Because of his age, his label held his royalties in trust until he was 21 and paid him $2.50 a week.
He was 13 when “Fingertips” topped the Billboard Hot 100, the youngest solo artist ever to top the chart.

7bhMBjjQhgPX0q9S4Ajncn.name: Ben Kweller
f: By the age of nine he had written a dozen songs and won an honourable mention in a songwriting contest sponsored by Billboard.
In 1993 he befriended drummer John Kent and formed the band Radish with bassist Ryan Green.
In 2003 he toured Australia with Ben Folds and Ben Lee as The Bens.

5PPCkoOKabpGGhqrUwSikz.name: Kimya Dawson
f: She co-founded the Moldy Peaches with Adam Green.
A version of “Anyone Else but You” sung by Michael Cera and Elliot Page charted on the Billboard Hot 100 after featuring in the 2007 film Juno.
Five of her solo songs and one Moldy Peaches track are on the Juno soundtrack, released in December 2007.

3oAbjWINfcTSAuVUlXXMty.name: Steve Forbert
f: After moving to New York in 1976 he busked in Greenwich Village and played early shows at the punk club CBGB.
He makes a cameo as Cyndi Lauper's boyfriend in the video for “Girls Just Want to Have Fun”.
Any Old Time, his tribute album to Jimmie Rodgers, was nominated for a 2004 Grammy in the Best Traditional Folk category.

4OTD2AbOu5iBqSWk3NfwG5.name: Getdown Services
f: Ben Sadler and Josh Law met at school in Minehead, Somerset, and are now based in Bristol.
In 2023 they signed with Bristol-based Breakfast Records and released their debut album, Crisps.
In 2026 they played London's Southbank Centre as part of the Meltdown festival curated by Harry Styles.

5wjWLK4KMqmRbdUtTEV1BG.name: Har Mar Superstar
f: The name comes from the Har Mar Mall, a shopping centre in Roseville, Minnesota.
He first performed as Har Mar in a choir robe, backed only by pre-recorded beats from a MiniDisc player.
After Britney Spears's management turned down his song “Tall Boy”, he recorded it himself for his album Dark Touches.

13jvSWmroZLlHV9cJqB5g4.name: Bobby Conn
f: Born Jeffrey Stafford in 1967, he performs as Bobby Conn and is based in Chicago.
At high school he started a hardcore punk trio, The Broken Kockamamies, whose only stage prop was a set of eight-foot strobe lights.
In 2003 he produced a session for the Cribs, who had supported him on a UK tour; part of it appeared on their 2004 debut.

6yjU0SoX3vxPV7KoopXlWe.name: Carole Bayer Sager
f: She wrote her first pop hit, “A Groovy Kind of Love”, with Toni Wine while still a student at New York's High School of Music and Art.
She wrote the lyrics to “Nobody Does It Better”, the Bond theme sung by Carly Simon in The Spy Who Loved Me (1977); Hamlisch composed the music.
She won the 1982 Academy Award for Best Original Song for “Arthur's Theme (Best That You Can Do)”.

1NpeO0rYdDwUjtaXMDlb25.name: Rob Moose
f: He left a master's programme in American studies at Columbia University to tour with Antony and the Johnsons in 2005.
Playing violin, viola, guitar and mandolin, he has performed on close to 500 albums.
He joined Bon Iver in 2011, arranging and recording the strings on their self-titled second album.

4XquDVA8pkg5Lx91No1JxB.name: Brittany Howard
f: After high school she worked for the United States Postal Service until becoming lead singer of Alabama Shakes full-time.
At Lollapalooza in 2015 she was invited on stage to sing “Get Back” as a duet with Paul McCartney.
In 2024 she co-wrote “Pale Pale Moon” with Ludwig Göransson; it featured prominently in Ryan Coogler's film Sinners.

1ZzqxDkqNDAJVaNO1xue3P.name: Fabiana Palladino
f: Born in central London, she is the daughter of Welsh musician Pino Palladino.
Jai Paul found her on SoundCloud while she was working in the Old Vic box office and signed her to his label, the Paul Institute.
In April 2025 it was announced that she had made production contributions to Lorde's fourth studio album, Virgin.

37uLId6Z5ZXCx19vuruvv5.name: Hot Chip
f: The band was formed around 2000 by Alexis Taylor and Joe Goddard, who had met as students at Elliott School, Putney.
Their second album, The Warning (2006), was nominated for the Mercury Prize.
“Ready for the Floor” was nominated for the Grammy for Best Dance Recording but lost to Daft Punk's “Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger (Alive 2007)”.

4x1nvY2FN8jxqAFA0DA02H.name: John Lennon
f: In 1956 he formed the Quarrymen, which became the Beatles in 1960.
In the mid-1960s he published In His Own Write and A Spaniard in the Works, collections of nonsense writing and line drawings.
As a performer, writer or co-writer he had 25 number-one singles on the Billboard Hot 100.

6Lll1MPPak4m4vZKuJB264.name: BRONCHO
f: The indie rock band formed in 2010 in Norman, Oklahoma.
Their song “It's On” played over the closing credits of the first episode of the third season of HBO's Girls.
“Boys Got to Go” was on the soundtrack of the 2019 football video game PES 2020.

4DLjEphXbW7qIhX4iwmNEe.name: Fat Dog
f: They formed during the COVID-19 lockdowns and, before releasing a single, were called “2023's wildest live band” by NME's Gary Ryan.
Drummer Johnny Hutch got the nickname “Doghead” from playing every gig with a latex dog mask on his head.
Frontman Joe Love has cited the music from Serious Sam as an influence on their sound, which mixes dance, punk and klezmer.

594LqcHtMvKoR0URmSiYJB.name: Syreeta
f: She joined Motown as a receptionist in 1965 and within a year was secretary to Mickey Stevenson.
She co-wrote Wonder's hit “Signed, Sealed, Delivered (I'm Yours)” and sang backing vocals on it.
Her first collaboration with Preston, “With You I'm Born Again”, reached number four in the US and number two in the UK in early 1980.

3fhOTtm0LBJ3Ojn4hIljLo.name: Roxy Music
f: Ferry picked Roxy from a list of old cinemas for its “faded glamour”, adding “Music” after learning of an American band called Roxy.
Robert Fripp and Peter Sinfield judged Ferry's voice unsuitable for King Crimson but helped Roxy Music get a recording contract with E.G. Records.
Manzanera did not make the band as guitarist at first, but impressed them enough to be invited to become their roadie.

5EOPLr73C9nIPYwVEAsiOY.name: Ed Harcourt
f: Before going solo he played bass and keyboards in Snug, a band formed at school in the mid-1990s.
In 2000 he recorded his debut mini-album, Maplewood EP, straight to a 4-track recorder at Wootton Manor.
He played piano with the Libertines when they were surprise guests on the Pyramid stage at Glastonbury on 26 June 2015.

1gxczmVzWKNJLz61uI27zJ.name: Evangeline
f: Evangeline is a Los Angeles indie singer-songwriter, formerly known as Eva B. Ross.

7fIfKG7oJGO4p8wvyi6adh.name: E.U.
f: E.U. stands for Experience Unlimited, a Washington, D.C. go-go and funk band fronted by singer and bassist Gregory “Sugar Bear” Elliot.
Beck sampled their track “Knock Him Out Sugar Ray” just before the second verse of “Where It's At”.
Public Enemy sampled their “E.U. Freeze” on the single “Night of the Living Baseheads”.

1SQRv42e4PjEYfPhS0Tk9E.name: The Kinks
f: Their breakthrough third single, Ray Davies's “You Really Got Me” (1964), topped the UK chart and reached the US Top 10.
Problems on their 1965 American tour led to the band being banned from touring the US for several years.
Rod Stewart, a fellow pupil at William Grimshaw school, was one of the early band's singers, performing with them at least once in early 1962.

2i1IdHG5w0wiSmJGoqAGlj.name: Minnie Riperton
f: She was known for her five-octave vocal range and her use of the whistle register.
Her group, by then a session group called Studio Three, sang backing vocals on Fontella Bass's 1965 hit “Rescue Me”.
In 1973 a college intern for Epic Records found her in semi-retirement.

4vjGlQWexbru6aOUCLTVir.name: Kiki Dee
f: She was the first female singer from the UK to sign with Motown's Tamla Records.
Songwriter Mitch Murray created her stage name and wrote her first single, “Early Night”.
Her 1976 duet with Elton John, “Don't Go Breaking My Heart”, reached number one in both the UK and the US.

20vuBdFblWUo2FCOvUzusB.name: David Byrne
f: Born in Dumbarton, Scotland, he co-founded Talking Heads in New York City in 1975.
His middle school choir rejected him for being “off-key and too withdrawn”.
With Brian Eno he made My Life in the Bush of Ghosts in 1979–81, an album noted for its early use of sampling and found sounds.

5lkiCO9UQ8B23dZ1o0UV4m.name: Jackson Browne
f: He was born in Heidelberg, Germany, in 1948.
Before he was 18 he was a staff writer in Greenwich Village for Elektra's publishing company, Nina Music.
Running on Empty (1977) was recorded entirely on tour, mixing new songs played live with recordings made on buses, in hotel rooms and backstage.

1yap1SgRPMxgyfrrDlQ95y.name: Emitt Rhodes
f: He recorded his self-titled 1970 album in his parents' garage, playing every instrument himself.
His musical and vocal style earned him the nickname “One-Man Beatles”.
In 2014 he began working with producer Chris Price; Rainbow Ends (2016) was his first album in 43 years.

22bE4uQ6baNwSHPVcDxLCe.name: The Rolling Stones
f: Mick Jagger and Keith Richards met again at Dartford railway station on 17 October 1961, when Jagger was carrying Chuck Berry and Muddy Waters records.
According to Richards, Jones named the band during a call to Jazz News after spotting the track “Rollin' Stone” on a Muddy Waters LP.
Their tongue and lips logo was created for Rolling Stones Records, the label they formed in 1970.

07Pw9XQo0hIwtKRrBwo0Rl.name: Brenda Fassie
f: Born in Langa, Cape Town, in 1964, she was named after the American singer Brenda Lee.
Time magazine called her “The Madonna of the Townships” in 2001.
Her album Memeza was the best-selling album in South Africa in 1998.

5eUda4BaWhUQWWJiP1ml5v.name: Sorry
f: The band formed in 2014 as Fish and changed their name to Sorry in 2016.
Before starting on original material, Lorenz and O'Bryen posted several covers of Jimi Hendrix songs.
In February 2021 they announced a live album recorded at the Windmill, Brixton, with proceeds going to the venue.

3f626JSVauIhTQgatsFcs4.name: Paul Williams
f: He wrote the lyrics to “Evergreen” from A Star Is Born, winning the Grammy for Song of the Year and the Academy Award for Best Original Song.
His song “We've Only Just Begun” was originally written for a Crocker National Bank TV commercial featuring newlyweds.
He co-wrote and sang on “Touch” and co-wrote “Beyond” on Daft Punk's album Random Access Memories.

6jlWj6y00bMQt8XoKuCjyZ.name: Emily King
f: She appeared on Nas's 2004 album Street's Disciple, credited simply as “Emily”.
Her first album, East Side Story (2007), was nominated for the Grammy for Best Contemporary R&B Album.
She helped compose and sang “Being Human”, the end theme of Cartoon Network's Steven Universe Future.

4wBhllC5Nto10UefzXVMt9.name: Omni
f: Guitarist Frankie Broyles was previously a member of Deerhunter and Balkans.
Their sound draws on post-punk bands such as Television, Talking Heads and Wire.
They signed to Sub Pop in 2019 and released their third album, Networker, that year.

5TjpsMnYz8lxTr91olqbEh.name: P.P. Arnold
f: She left the Ike & Tina Turner Revue in autumn 1966, after a UK tour with the Rolling Stones, and went solo in London with Mick Jagger's encouragement.
She sang backing vocals on the Small Faces' hits “Itchycoo Park” and “Tin Soldier”.
The Nice, with Keith Emerson on organ, followed the Blue Jays as her backing band.

62sC6lUEWRjbFqXpMmOk4G.name: Fugazi
f: MacKaye took the word “fugazi”, meaning false or inauthentic, from Mark Baker's Nam, a book of Vietnam War veterans' stories.
MacKaye's original idea for the band was “MC5 plus reggae”.
Ertegun offered them their own label and more than $10 million just to sign with Atlantic; they declined.

7K48RaFMB6BhTLc0KspbTh.name: Daryl Johns
f: Daryl Johns is from New Jersey, in the United States.

4CxobvwTpmfpIEbkYh4pAb.name: Eric Johnson
f: His violin-like lead sound came from a 1954 Fender Stratocaster he named Virginia.
He recorded his debut album, Seven Worlds, in Austin in 1976–78; after contract disputes it was not released until 1998.
He worked as a session guitarist for Cat Stevens, Carole King and Christopher Cross.

3sFhA6G1N0gG1pszb6kk1m.name: Wings
f: They went through three lead guitarists and four drummers, while the core trio of the McCartneys and Denny Laine stayed throughout.
On the first tour by an ex-Beatle after the split, Wings played no Beatles songs.
They had six number-one singles on the Billboard Hot 100.

2Jv5eshHtLycR6R8KQCdc4.name: Grizzly Bear
f: The name began in the early 2000s as a moniker for songwriter Ed Droste's own music.
Their 2009 album Veckatimest is named after a tiny, uninhabited island on Cape Cod that the band visited.
On their last date touring with Radiohead, in Toronto, Jonny Greenwood called Grizzly Bear his favourite band from the stage.

4nymPwNq7Y6i1tVs1d9WVB.name: The Free Design
f: The original line-up was all Dedricks: Chris, his sister Sandy and his brother Bruce.
Their work later influenced Belle and Sebastian, Stereolab, Cornelius, Pizzicato Five and Beck.
In 2000 they regrouped after nearly 30 years to record “Endless Harmony” for a Beach Boys tribute album.

2wAPeWKKHrPZ3UUqnw9Bpy.name: Connie Converse
f: Her 1950s songs are among the earliest known recordings in the US singer-songwriter genre.
Her only known public performance was a brief 1954 appearance on CBS's The Morning Show with Walter Cronkite.
Before and after her songwriting years she was an academic and editor, including of the Journal of Conflict Resolution at the University of Michigan.

18RkLKfeoUgZflWv9os25W.name: Miriam Makeba
f: She was nicknamed Mama Africa.
With Harry Belafonte she won the Grammy for Best Folk Recording for their 1965 album An Evening with Belafonte/Makeba.
She said she learned to sing in English before she could speak it.

4Ajgo7nAsTzjSFymIfBjZ1.name: The Felice Brothers
f: From Palenville in the Catskills, they started out playing in New York's 42nd Street and Union Square subway stations.
When storms cut the power at the Newport Folk Festival, they played their set unplugged.
Their “Radio Song” plays on the bar jukebox in the 2017 film Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri.

1HkQ4XrPffqcVW0TgTTw0d.name: Yma Sumac
f: Born Zoila Emperatriz Chávarri Castillo, she took her stage name from the Quechua “Ima sumaq”, meaning “how beautiful”.
In 1956 she won a Guinness World Record for the Greatest Range of Musical Value.
Her debut album, Voice of the Xtabay (1950), reached number one on the Billboard 200 and sold a million copies in the US.

7sECLFfpeGHQYRH7Lvc9pA.name: Arthur Lee
f: In 1965 his folk rock group the Grass Roots renamed itself Love because another signed act already had that name.
Love's 1967 album Forever Changes is in the Grammy Hall of Fame and the National Recording Registry.
He said he wanted a guitarist with a Curtis Mayfield–like feel for a session, and label owner Billy Revis recommended Jimi Hendrix.

1bAdBYcsDdsbqmWbAE7qKR.name: JJ
f: They met in their hometown of Vallentuna, outside Stockholm, and began playing together at a local youth centre.
Their song “My Life” was used in an official Battlefield 3 trailer in April 2011.
In 2011 they released “We Can't Stop” with Ne-Yo as part of Adult Swim's Singles Program.

4bthk9UfsYUYdcFyqxmSUU.name: Tears For Fears
f: Curt Smith and Roland Orzabal formed the band in Bath in 1981 after their mod-influenced first band, Graduate, split.
The duo were first called History of Headaches; the name Tears for Fears was inspired by psychologist Arthur Janov's primal therapy.
Local musician Ian Stanley gave them free use of his home 8-track studio and became their keyboard player.

3C8RpaI3Go0yFF9whvKoED.name: The Avalanches
f: Three future members formed Alarm 115, a Melbourne noise punk band, in 1994.
They borrowed their name from an American surf rock band whose only album was Ski Surfin' with the Avalanches (1963).
Robbie Chater estimated that Since I Left You was assembled from about 3,500 vinyl samples.

66uU7VPJQ8eC06LAZyqYYk.name: Dead Man's Bones
f: Gosling and Shields met in 2005 and discovered a shared obsession with the Haunted Mansion ride at Disneyland.
Their first album was made with the Silverlake Conservatory Children's Choir, started by Red Hot Chili Peppers bassist Flea.
They played every instrument on the record, even ones they had never touched, with no click track and aiming for no more than three takes a song.

6f1YthbbEpu9qHzOUW2UYI.name: Tonight
f: They were a five-piece new wave band from Southend-on-Sea, active from June 1977 to January 1979.
With the Rich Kids, they were the first acts called power pop, a term Charles Catchpole first used in the Evening Standard on 17 January 1978.
Their album Drummerman was shelved by WEA in 1978 and finally released in 2010 by Angel Air Records.

6CFQDzNLNcuK5lVZ766Yxt.name: Yannis
f: He is a founding member and the lead singer of Foals, with whom he has released seven studio albums since 2005.
His project Yannis & The Yaw released the EP Lagos Paris London, made with Nigerian musician Tony Allen, on 30 August 2024.
In January 2018 he started MILK, a monthly south London club night whose special guests are kept secret until the night.

3PP6ghmOlDl2jaKaH0avUN.name: Black Country, New Road
f: Isaac Wood suggested the name, a road in the West Midlands, after using an online encyclopedia's random-article button.
Their debut album, For the First Time (2021), was nominated for the Mercury Prize and reached No. 4 on the UK Albums Chart.
Physical copies of their first two singles, including 2019's “Sunglasses”, were reportedly resold for over £100.

4T4JE09FOmRgv2Wzb6JaOR.name: Willie J Healey
f: He first planned to be a boxer and, before his record deal, earned money as a plasterer in Carterton.
He says Jamie T lent him a drum machine during lockdown, which led to the more funk-based sound of his album Bunny.
He added the “J” because “Willie Healey” on its own “sounded like it needed something going on in the middle”.

0Mz5XE0kb1GBnbLQm2VbcO.name: Mos Def
f: Born Dante Terrell Smith in 1973, he is now known as Yasiin Bey.
In 1996 he and fellow Brooklyn rapper Talib Kweli formed the duo Black Star.
Around the time of Black on Both Sides, he also contributed to the Scritti Politti album Anomie & Bonhomie.

1HOeqtP7tHkKNJNLzQ2tnr.name: Everything Everything
f: The name comes from the first two words of Radiohead's “Everything in Its Right Place”, the opening track of Kid A.
Their work has twice been shortlisted for the Mercury Prize and has received five Ivor Novello nominations.
Higgs and Pritchard first played together in Salford math rock trio Modern Bison, whose only album was I Could Have Had a Rustic Pagoda (2006).

4MGA6AM4iZ2HYc6b77og9g.name: Dirty Nice
f: They are a British band with Charlie Pelling on lead vocals, alongside Mark Thompson.

4UvhuGdFf75Cfan7lEU1J1.name: The Books
f: Zammuto and de Jong met in 1999 in a shared New York apartment building, where de Jong played Zammuto samples including a Shooby Taylor record.
In 2004 the French Ministry of Culture asked them to compose music for a new lift in its building.
Before a three-month North American tour in April 2006, they had played only one concert, at a Chicago festival in October 2003.

5GGJosGMs08YEmKTZJe1fL.name: Suki Waterhouse
f: She played keyboardist Karen Sirko in the 2023 series Daisy Jones & the Six.
“Good Looking”, one of her singles from 2017–2019, became a viral hit in 2022.
In August 2024 she opened for Taylor Swift's Eras Tour at Wembley Stadium.

54KCNI7URCrG6yjQK3Ukow.name: Susanne Sundfør
f: Her 2010 album The Brothel reached number one in Norway and became the best-selling album of that year.
Her instrumental album A Night at Salle Pleyel is a live recording of a piece for synthesisers alone, commissioned for the Oslo Jazz Festival's 25th anniversary.
She released “Running to the Sea”, a collaboration with Norwegian electronic duo Röyksopp.

5X3TuTi9OIsJXMGxPwTKM2.name: The Young Rascals
f: They dropped an earlier name, Them, because a UK group including Van Morrison was using it, and found the Rascals name with help from TV comedian Soupy Sales.
To promote them, the phrase ‘The Rascals are coming!’ was posted on the Shea Stadium scoreboard at the Beatles' 1965 tour opener.
The ‘Young’ was added after the Harmonica Rascals objected to them releasing records as the Rascals.

77tT1kLj6mCWtFNqiOmP9H.name: Daryl Hall & John Oates
f: Daryl Hall and John Oates first met at the Adelphi Ballroom in Philadelphia in 1967, each leading his own group: the Temptones and the Masters.
Their nickname came from a shared apartment whose mailbox read ‘Hall & Oates’.
Six of their singles reached number one, from ‘Rich Girl’ (1977) to ‘Out of Touch’ (1984).

32vWCbZh0xZ4o9gkz4PsEU.name: Dolly Parton
f: She wrote her first song at six and became a professional songwriter at sixteen.
At thirteen she recorded ‘Puppy Love’ for Goldband Records and appeared at the Grand Ole Opry, where she first met Johnny Cash.
She had 44 Top 10 country albums, a record for any artist, and 25 No. 1 Billboard country singles.

1667U2YoucgG5Pdvm2M59c.name: Orleans
f: The name came from the music they played when they formed, inspired partly by Louisiana artists including Allen Toussaint and the Neville Brothers.
Rolling Stone once called them ‘the best unrecorded band in America’.
ABC refused to release Orleans II in the US, saying it had ‘no hit singles’, though it contained the first recording of ‘Dance With Me’.

6hAUCkzZpoYGObd8qFW5TT.name: Pokey LaFarge
f: He was born Andrew Heissler in Bloomington, Illinois.
After hearing Bill Monroe at 16, he traded his guitar for a mandolin.
He and his band the South City Three played on ‘I Guess I Should Go To Sleep’ from Jack White's 2012 album Blunderbuss.

1bSCGVnnijnSf8R9maUeJ9.name: Camille Yarbrough
f: A vocal sample from the opening of her ‘Take Yo’ Praise' features prominently in Fatboy Slim's 1999 song ‘Praise You’.
Her album The Iron Pot Cooker was based on a 1971 staging of her one-woman spoken-word show, Tales and Tunes of an African American Griot.
In her teens she danced with the Katherine Dunham Company.

3lnWfdMG9U0oVMC15SEbB5.name: BODEGA
f: The band is named after the term New Yorkers use for small corner shops.
Their first full-length album, Endless Scroll (2018), was produced by Parquet Courts member Austin Brown and released on What's Your Rupture?
The New York band formed on 28 July 2016.

6jQ9UtYXqNfVnPkrH1Xxwi.name: Maxine Nightingale
f: At thirteen she began singing with a band called Unisound, performing widely on the British cabaret circuit.
From 1969 she spent about 18 months in the West End production of Hair, understudying the lead role of Sheila.
Her single ‘Lead Me On’ reached No. 1 on Billboard's Easy Listening chart in the US in July 1979.

3M8NUieZuEOMs0Hf210w4n.name: Van Dyke Parks
f: In the early 1950s, at the American Boychoir School in Princeton, he sang under conductors Arturo Toscanini, Thomas Beecham and Eugene Ormandy.
His arrangements for Disney soundtracks include ‘The Bare Necessities’ for The Jungle Book (1967).
He worked with Brian Wilson on the Beach Boys' Smile, which Wilson later completed as a solo album in 2004.

6i6WlGzQtXtz7GcC5H5st5.name: 10cc
f: Strawberry Studios got its name in October 1968, from the Beatles' ‘Strawberry Fields Forever’.
Graham Gouldman made his name writing hits for other acts, including ‘For Your Love’, ‘Bus Stop’ and ‘No Milk Today’.
Kevin Godley and Lol Creme left in 1976 to develop an electronic music device called ‘The Gizmo’.

485uL27bPomh29R4JmQehQ.name: Bob Seger
f: His first original song, ‘The Lonely One’, recorded with his band the Decibels at Del Shannon's studio in 1961, aired once on an Ann Arbor station.
He co-wrote the Eagles' number-one hit ‘Heartache Tonight’.
‘Shakedown’, written for the 1987 film Beverly Hills Cop II, topped the Billboard Hot 100.

0Wkm45quqfx3NepJpXDvwE.name: Superorganism
f: Working remotely, Noguchi was sent a GarageBand instrumental file and returned her deadpan vocals, recorded on her MacBook's built-in microphone.
Their first single, ‘Something For Your M.I.N.D.’, was later on the FIFA 18 soundtrack.
Soul (Earl Ho) was the only member living apart from the group, in Sydney; an enlarged image of his face often took his place in group photos.

57kIMCLPgkzQlXjblX7XXP.name: Phosphorescent
f: Phosphorescent is Matthew Houck from Huntsville, Alabama, who began recording under the name in 2001 in Athens, Georgia.
Before becoming Phosphorescent he toured as Fillup Shack and self-released a limited pressing of the album Hipolit in 2000.
Inspired by Willie Nelson's Lefty Frizzell tribute To Lefty from Willie, he made a Nelson tribute, To Willie, in 2009.

0JqRJZzARcjmH60HwUenow.name: Fox Academy
f: The band's original members are Micheal Todd Berland and Christian Novelli.

62pBNClOEZJEyRXrzC2CtI.name: The Apache Relay
f: The band took its name from a race-competition scene in the film Heavyweights.
Formed in a dorm at Belmont University, they released the concept album 1988 in 2009 as Michael Ford Jr. & the Apache Relay.
They released ‘Katie Queen of Tennessee’ as a single in 2014, from their self-titled album.

19eLuQmk9aCobbVDHc6eek.name: Louis Armstrong
f: Around 1922 he followed his mentor Joe ‘King’ Oliver to Chicago to play in Oliver's Creole Jazz Band.
He made three albums with Ella Fitzgerald: Ella and Louis (1956), Ella and Louis Again (1957) and Porgy and Bess (1959).
His recording of ‘Melancholy Blues’ is on the Voyager Golden Record, sent into space.

3uuQLSmKyXSXIStTYGKLrT.name: Freddie Scott
f: In 1962 he cut Goffin and King's ‘Hey, Girl’ as a demo for Chuck Jackson, then recorded it himself when Jackson missed the session.
His recording of Berns's ‘Are You Lonely for Me’ reputedly took over 100 takes, then spent four weeks at the top of the R&B chart.
His 1968 song ‘(You) Got What I Need’ was sampled for Biz Markie's 1989 hit ‘Just a Friend’ and Ghostface Killah's ‘Save Me Dear’ (2004).

3mC1KCuZZSOlN8Z0M56VsV.name: Dobie Gray
f: Sonny Bono steered him to Stripe Records, which suggested the name Dobie Gray as a nod to the sitcom The Many Loves of Dobie Gillis.
He recorded ‘Drift Away’ at Quadrafonic Sound Studios, co-owned by Norbert Putnam and David Briggs, with a guitar riff by Reggie Young.
In 1970 he joined the band Pollution as singer and percussionist; they were managed by Beverly Hillbillies actor Max Baer Jr.

3dkbV4qihUeMsqN4vBGg93.name: Al Green
f: Producer Willie Mitchell hired him in 1969 to sing at a Texas show with his band, then asked him to sign with Hi Records.
He dropped the final ‘e’ from his name before releasing his first album on Hi Records.
Rolling Stone ranked him No. 10 on its 2023 list of the 200 Greatest Singers of All Time.

0SwO7SWeDHJijQ3XNS7xEE.name: MGMT
f: They started out as The Management and shortened it to MGMT because another band was already using the name.
When Columbia Records' A&R department called to say it was interested, the band thought it was a joke.
They opened for Paul McCartney, an admitted fan, at Fenway Park in Boston on 5 and 6 August 2009.

320TrJub4arztwXRm7kqVO.name: Dr. John
f: At about 13 he met Professor Longhair and soon began performing with him.
The Dr. John identity was first meant for Barron to front, but Barron dropped out and he took over the role himself.
In Los Angeles in the 1960s and 1970s he was a ‘first call’ session musician and part of the Wrecking Crew.

0K1q0nXQ8is36PzOKAMbNe.name: Spoon
f: Britt Daniel and Jim Eno formed the band in late 1993 after meeting as members of the Alien Beats.
The name honours the German krautrock band Can, whose hit ‘Spoon’ was the US theme song for the 1985 film Jagged Edge.
In 2009 the review aggregator Metacritic named Spoon its ‘Top overall artist of the decade’.

7vpRSadEAzLs0ikY7gAESe.name: Hamilton, Joe Frank & Reynolds
f: All three original members had played in the T-Bones, a 1960s band known for the instrumental hit “No Matter What Shape (Your Stomach's In)”.
Signing them in late 1974, Playboy Records made them keep the name though Reynolds had left; within months they released the Hot 100 number one “Fallin' in Love”.
WABC DJ Dan Ingram had a running joke introducing them as “Hamilton, Joe, Frank Reynolds and the entire Eyewitness News team”.

08GQAI4eElDnROBrJRGE0X.name: Fleetwood Mac
f: Green and Fleetwood named the band Fleetwood Mac to entice McVie to join on bass, but he chose to keep his steady income with Mayall.
They made their debut on 13 August 1967 at the National Jazz and Blues Festival, billed as “Peter Green's Fleetwood Mac featuring Jeremy Spencer”.
Their single “Black Magic Woman” later became a big hit when Santana covered it.

5cMVRrisBpDkXCVG48epED.name: Jenny Lewis
f: As a child actress in the 1980s she appeared in the films Troop Beverly Hills and The Wizard, both released in 1989.
She wanted to name the group Love's Way, after her parents' lounge act in Las Vegas, but Sennett “didn't go for it”.
Asked by Blake Sennett to sing backing vocals, she refused to join the band unless she could sing lead.

2vQavlZtDA660mnZotYIto.name: Link Wray
f: “Rumble” was banned in New York and Boston for fear it would incite teenage gang violence.
Pete Townshend of the Who once said he would never have picked up a guitar if it hadn't been for Wray and “Rumble”.
He is credited with inventing the power chord.

5g2n2H9ndqvejERtwZ1rHh.name: The Rascals
f: Their $15,000 deal made them the first white-only act signed to Atlantic Records, then a label of mainly black artists.
As a publicity stunt, “The Rascals are coming!” was posted on the Shea Stadium scoreboard as the Beatles opened their 1965 North American tour.
They became the Young Rascals because another act, the Harmonica Rascals, objected to them recording as the Rascals.

3GHKajYkw1Btlzib5wRpHf.name: Innovations
f: They were a 1970s Peruvian new wave pop and soft rock group.
Members included Javier Guerrero on keyboards and lead vocals and Ernesto Samamé on bass.

2jgPkn6LuUazBoBk6vvjh5.name: The Zombies
f: Originally the Mustangs, they became the Zombies at Arnold's suggestion; Blunstone admitted he didn't really know what a zombie was.
In May 1964 they won a £250 prize in a beat-group competition organised by Watford Borough Council.
Their first hit, “She's Not There”, peaked at No. 12 in the UK, their only UK Top 40 hit, but climbed to No. 2 in the US.

5dHfLBNU8zoypgKefzEB1c.name: Pomplamoose
f: Their name comes from a misspelling of the French word pamplemousse, meaning grapefruit.
Formed in 2008 by Jack Conte and Nataly Dawn, the duo sold about 100,000 songs online in 2009.
In September 2010 they recorded “Jungle Animal” with Allee Willis, who offered to write them a song after hearing their cover of Earth, Wind & Fire's “September”.

3ir2pF2mkiEWqyPenKTh5e.name: Indigo De Souza
f: She started making music at nine, and her first release, the EP Boys, was recorded in a friend's garage.
She self-released her first album, I Love My Mom, in 2018; Saddle Creek Records discovered it and gave it a proper release in 2021.
On her song “Real Pain” she put recordings of crowdsourced screams in the chorus.

0vIme0FGc4SmFByKiV27tw.name: ARTHUR
f: ARTHUR is a musician based in Pennsylvania.

04PoYcw0Zcevr7MQC0kzUM.name: bby
f: The band started in London in 2023.
Its members are Benjy Gibson, Deon Graham, Jessy Jacquet-Cretides, Tommy Medica and Tom Parkin.

2IU5UBup85LmAXh5U36DeC.name: The Grass Roots
f: The name originated in mid-1965 for a band project by Los Angeles songwriting and production duo P.F. Sloan and Steve Barri.
Entner, who had attended UCLA film school alongside future Doors members Jim Morrison and Ray Manzarek, met fellow busker Creed Bratton in Israel in 1965.
Their first top-10 hit, “Let's Live for Today” (1967), was an English-language cover of “Piangi con me” by the Anglo-Italian band the Rokes.

2hO4YtXUFJiUYS2uYFvHNK.name: Traveling Wilburys
f: Harrison joked to Lynne about recording errors caused by faulty equipment: “We'll bury 'em in the mix.”
The members took tongue-in-cheek pseudonyms as half-brothers from the fictional Wilbury family of travelling musicians.
Harrison, Lynne and Petty went to see Orbison at the Celebrity Theatre in Anaheim and recruited him shortly before he went on stage.

0e86yPdC41PGRkLp2Q1Bph.name: Mother Mother
f: Ryan Guldemond started the band in Heriot Bay, British Columbia, in January 2005 while at music school, recruiting his sister Molly.
Their self-titled debut, released under the name Mother with a three-headed rooster on the cover, was reissued in 2007 as Touch Up with a five-headed rooster.
Last Gang Records signed them after a 2006 Pop Montreal set and urged them to change their name from Mother to avoid legal issues.

23E65IfLBGQv0FBrMwCcG2.name: Peter McPoland
f: An acoustic version of “Romeo and Juliet” that he posted on TikTok in March 2021 gathered over a million views; that May he signed to Columbia Records.
His 2023 album Piggy takes its title from a main character in the novel Lord of the Flies.
He produced, engineered and played every part of his second album, Big Lucky (2025), his first independent release after leaving Columbia.

2kGBy2WHvF0VdZyqiVCkDT.name: Father John Misty
f: In 2008 he joined Fleet Foxes as their drummer, and played on their second album, Helplessness Blues (2011).
After moving to Seattle at 21, he worked at a bakery, recording music at night before his 4:30 am shift.
As a producer and songwriter he has contributed to albums by Beyoncé, Lady Gaga, Kid Cudi, Lana Del Rey and Post Malone.

6eJa3zG1QZLRB3xgRuyxbm.name: Dayglow
f: Dayglow is the project of Sloan Struble, who took the name from the song “Day Glo” by Brazos.
Although he is its only member, Struble calls Dayglow a band rather than a solo act, likening it to Tame Impala or Mutemath.
At 11, Struble began teaching himself guitar, bass, keyboard, synthesiser and drums, and how to produce and mix, using GarageBand.

7xxsnuyDlv8QUCHLZd2Qlz.name: Outer Limits Recordings
f: Outer Limits Recordings was Sam Mehran's alias from 2010, associated with the early hypnagogic pop and chillwave scene.
Mehran named his main influences as Ariel Pink, R. Stevie Moore and “basically most music that was recorded before 1990”.
The project issued numerous cassettes and limited-edition vinyl discs and, by Mehran's account, lasted until “somewhere in the spring of 2011”.

147s6QtLc4KPRmh5YxfpMO.name: Sam Mehran
f: He founded Test Icicles with Rory Attwell and Devonté Hynes in 2004.
His first album as Matrix Metals, Flamingo Breeze, was described as a pioneering work of vaporwave.
He co-wrote and co-produced Katie Rush's Law of Attraction (2014), then produced Puro Instinct's Autodrama (2016) and Samantha Urbani's Policies of Power (2017).

3WKTiixhkaWRexRUs3GKBw.name: Alan Price
f: He was a founder of the Alan Price Combo, later renamed the Animals, and played organ on “The House of the Rising Sun”.
He composed the soundtrack to Lindsay Anderson's 1973 film O Lucky Man!
His second album, A Price on His Head (1967), featured seven songs by Randy Newman, then virtually unknown.

7d7q5Y1p2QWS4QRAhTQR5E.name: Anne Murray
f: She was the first Canadian female solo singer to reach No. 1 in the US, and the first to earn a gold record, for “Snowbird” (1970).
After graduating in 1966, she taught physical education for a year at a high school in Summerside, Prince Edward Island.
She has won a record 25 Juno Awards, as well as four Grammys.

4chuPfKtATDZvbRLExsTp2.name: Vashti Bunyan
f: She was expelled from the Ruskin School of Drawing and Fine Art at Oxford in 1964 for learning guitar and writing songs instead of art.
Her first single, the Jagger–Richards song “Some Things Just Stick in Your Mind”, came out in June 1965 with Jimmy Page on guitar.
By 2000 her album had a cult following and was reissued; she returned to recording after a 30-year gap, releasing Lookaftering in 2005 and Heartleap in 2014.

3HC7NcxQx2Yk0fWoRKJ0xF.name: Jefferson Starship
f: Blows Against the Empire, the album on which Kantner and Slick sang of escaping Earth in a hijacked starship, was nominated for a Hugo Award in 1971.
Their album Red Octopus went double platinum and reached No. 1 on the Billboard 200 in 1975.

3Q6OOkfssqoMSTtl11J5Uk.name: Love
f: Led by songwriter Arthur Lee, they were one of the first racially diverse American rock bands.
The band was first called the Grass Roots, but Lee renamed it Love when another group of that name appeared.
In 1964 Lee wrote and produced Rosa Lee Brooks's single “My Diary”, which featured Jimi Hendrix on guitar.

76o4kCpWMmBGl8jIYfRHTk.name: Ken Dodd
f: As a singer he sold more than 100 million records.
He made his professional debut in September 1954 at the Nottingham Empire as Professor Yaffle Chucklebutty, Operatic Tenor and Sausage Knotter.
In the 1960s he set a Guinness record for the longest joke-telling session: 1,500 jokes in three and a half hours at Liverpool's Royal Court Theatre.

6PAt558ZEZl0DmdXlnjMgD.name: Eric Clapton
f: His nickname “Slowhand” came from Giorgio Gomelsky, a pun on the slow handclapping that followed when he stopped playing to replace a string.
He first played the Royal Albert Hall with the Yardbirds in December 1964 and has since performed there over 200 times.
He is the only three-time inductee to the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame: as a solo artist, and with the Yardbirds and Cream.

2G8UkPZnQ8i78L8TfqP1X6.name: Christian Leave
f: Born Christian Akridge and raised in Wichita Falls, Texas, he fronts a band named after his social media username.
Before making music he joined Vine in 2014, aged 14, and gained more than 800,000 followers.
His first EP, Hope, released on 1 July 2016, debuted at number 48 on Billboard's Independent Albums chart.

3eskO5m0H4yiF64vRySBjr.name: Buffalo Springfield
f: The band took its name from a steamroller made by the Buffalo-Springfield Roller Company.
On 6 April 1966 Stills and Richie Furay spotted Neil Young and Bruce Palmer stuck in traffic on Sunset Boulevard, heading the other way.
Stephen Stills went on to form Crosby, Stills and Nash with David Crosby of the Byrds and Graham Nash of the Hollies.

4vpDg7Y7fU982Ds30zawDA.name: The Band
f: From 1958 to 1963 they were the Hawks, backing band for rockabilly singer Ronnie Hawkins in Toronto.
Hudson's condition for agreeing was that the Hawks each pay him $10 a week to be their instructor and buy a new Lowrey organ.
They backed Bob Dylan on his 1966 concert tour as his first electric band.

0oSGxfWSnnOXhD2fKuz2Gy.name: David Bowie
f: He got a Grafton saxophone in 1961 and was soon taking lessons from baritone saxophonist Ronnie Ross.
From 1988 to 1992 he fronted the hard rock band Tin Machine.
He created “Bowie Bonds”, the first modern celebrity bond.

48c9PKsgH8QMkAN6pg6Xz8.name: Chaparelle
f: The group comes from Austin and started in 2023.
Its members are Beau Bedford, Zella Day and Jesse Woods.

100sLnojEpcadRx4edEBA6.name: Zella Day
f: She released her debut album, Powered by Love, independently in 2009 at the age of 14.
Her cover of the White Stripes' “Seven Nation Army” reached number one on Hype Machine's charts and passed 50 million Spotify plays.
Since 2023 she has been a member of the country group Chaparelle.

5I6MzhNEMk27cZsCqGAIYo.name: The Youngbloods
f: The band's name referred to Young's second album.
Their first concert was at Gerde's Folk City in Greenwich Village; months later they were the house band at the Cafe Au Go Go.
Their only US Top 40 entry was Chet Powers's “Get Together”.

4qmHkMxr6pTWh5Zo74odpH.name: Elvis Costello & The Attractions
f: This Year's Model (1978) was Costello's first album with the Attractions; he had used the American band Clover on his debut, My Aim Is True.
Bassist Bruce Thomas and drummer Pete Thomas are no relation.
The group was active from 1977 to 1996, with Elvis Costello, Steve Nieve, Bruce Thomas and Pete Thomas as members.

3d2pb1dHTm8b61zAGVUVvO.name: Mick Jagger
f: He starred in the 1970 films Performance and Ned Kelly.
He studied at the London School of Economics before leaving to focus on the Rolling Stones.
On 17 October 1961 he met Richards again at Dartford station; the Chuck Berry and Muddy Waters records he was carrying revealed a shared interest in R&B.

1QyjHJQb3WeWFxXaNLpLOw.name: Anna Ash
f: Anna Ash comes from Michigan.

1gR0gsQYfi6joyO1dlp76N.name: Justice
f: Their first tracks together were for Musclorvision's “Hits Up to You”, a compilation of songs designed to sound like Eurovision entries.
They first came to prominence with a 2003 remix of Simian's “Never Be Alone”, made for a Paris college radio station's remix contest.
Their remix of MGMT's “Electric Feel” won the 2009 Grammy Award for Best Remixed Recording, Non-Classical.

5INjqkS1o8h1imAzPqGZBb.name: Tame Impala
f: In the studio, Parker writes, records, performs and produces the project's music.
It began in 2007 as Parker's home-recording project, with tracks posted on Myspace.
A remix of the single “Dracula” with Jennie of Blackpink became the project's first top-ten hit on the US Billboard Hot 100.

1GiGmnJBIwKiXV8AbjuJ9P.name: Life in Film
f: The band formed when singer Samuel Fry returned to London from studying in Bournemouth and teamed up with old school friend Edward Ibbotson.
Their song “Alleyway” was the first track chosen to front Burberry's Burberry Acoustic initiative.
Veteran indie producer Stephen Street worked with them on their debut album, released in 2015.

0h1gX589xBKUCijeC8Bewy.name: Charlotte Adigéry
f: In 2016 she sang on “The Best Thing” from the soundtrack to the film Belgica, scored by Soulwax's David and Stephen Dewaele.
Her Creole-language track “Paténipat” was used in the trailer for HBO's 2020 series The New Pope.
She also records as WWWater, a rawer, more punk project.

0dSnTqwXok006MwsjjlzUl.name: Bolis Pupul
f: He played in the synthpop band Hong Kong Dong with his sister and her husband.
His solo debut album, Letter to Yu, was released on 8 March 2024.

5hE6NCoobhyEu6TRSbjOJY.name: Fever Ray
f: Fever Ray comes from Nacka, Sweden.

13peDbMKVZpn5nanRC96WJ.name: Thumpasaurus
f: Thumpasaurus is a funk band from Los Angeles, formed in 2015.
Its members include Logan Kane.

2dBj3prW7gP9bCCOIQeDUf.name: Danger Mouse
f: He took his name from the English cartoon series Danger Mouse and performed in a mouse outfit because he was too shy to show his face.
While living in New Cross, London, and working at the Rose pub near London Bridge, he sent a demo to Lex Records, which signed him.
His 2004 release The Grey Album combined Jay-Z's vocals from The Black Album with instrumentals from the Beatles' album The Beatles.

4fUoc6Qd6emrChaXSkS91n.name: Jemini
f: The rapper's collaborations with Danger Mouse were the first original releases Danger Mouse issued under that name.

320EPCSEezHt1rtbfwH6Ck.name: The Monkees
f: Television producers Bob Rafelson and Bert Schneider conceived the group in 1965 for an NBC sitcom of the same name.
Michael Nesmith, Peter Tork and Micky Dolenz were picked for the show's cast from 437 applicants.
The band had three number-one singles: “Last Train to Clarksville”, “I'm a Believer” and “Daydream Believer”.

2kRFetyCeU3r24DVyTZVFx.name: Surfbort
f: Vocalist Dani Miller formed the band in Brooklyn, New York, in 2014.
The band took its name from the Beyoncé song “Drunk in Love”.
They featured in Gucci's Pre-Fall 2019 campaign, photographed in Sicily.

1jFVu6Z7wmwywivOeBTSIV.name: Miya Folick
f: A high-school friend taught her to play guitar during a gap semester.
Her debut album, Premonitions, came out on 26 October 2018.
In 2022 she featured on American Football's cover of “Fade Into You”.

2VPvWVAiP9GICmwh4bLUuE.name: Sahara Hotnights
f: The line-up has never changed: singer Maria Andersson, drummer Josephine Forsman and sisters Jennie (lead guitar) and Johanna (bass) Asplund.
Forsman named the band after a horse called Sahara Hotnights that she bet on while in Australia.
“Alright Alright (Here's My Fist Where's the Fight?)” is used in Cheaper by the Dozen, Stormbreaker, New York Minute and on the Jackass: The Movie soundtrack.

5mZC7ndY6oGMxJentRwsuV.name: Young Fathers
f: Before becoming Young Fathers in 2008, the trio released a single as 3Style in 2005.
They won the 2014 Mercury Prize for their debut album, Dead.
The band composed the soundtrack for the 2025 horror film 28 Years Later.

7kAZYW5e5hQHYGQ0XHYhns.name: Mustard Service
f: The band formed after lead singer Marco Rivero was kicked out of a previous band he shared with Augusto Di Catarina and Armando Baeza.
The name Mustard Service came from a band name generator.
In autumn 2018 they joined the Madrid band Hinds on a sixteen-date US tour.

12fRkVfO2fUsz1QHgDAG3g.name: Julia Jacklin
f: She worked in an essential oils factory to pay for recording with producer Ben Edwards, having been inspired by Aldous Harding's debut album.
In 2014 she formed the indie garage group Phantastic Ferniture with Elizabeth Hughes on guitar and Ryan K Brennan on drums.
In 2025 she became lead vocalist of Binspoon, a Grinspoon tribute act.

0Lpr5wXzWLtDWm1SjNbpPb.name: Todd Rundgren
f: He organised the first interactive television concert in 1978, designed the first colour graphics tablet in 1980 and made the first interactive album, No World Order, in 1993.
He wrote both sides of Nazz's debut single, July 1968's “Open My Eyes” backed with “Hello It's Me”.
As a producer he worked on the New York Dolls' self-titled debut album and Grand Funk Railroad's We're an American Band.

5O35zGUolf87RATk2NgSD3.name: Hether
f: Hether is Paul Castelluzzo, a US musician, producer and songwriter from Los Angeles.

2u7xZP39dtED9EuRX9MUwu.name: Orange Juice
f: They began in 1976 as the Nu Sonics, named after the affordable Burns Nu-Sonic guitar played by Edwyn Collins.
Their first singles came out in the early 1980s on Postcard Records, an independent label founded by Edwyn Collins and Alan Horne.
Fewer than 1,000 copies of their single ‘Falling and Laughing’ were pressed, 200 of them with a postcard by the band.

4Q82S0VzF8qlCb4PnSDurj.name: Brian Wilson
f: After signing with Capitol Records in 1962, he became the first pop musician credited for writing, arranging, producing and performing his own material.
A portable two-track Wollensak tape recorder, given to him for his 16th birthday, let him experiment with recording songs and group vocals.
He named an early group with his cousin Mike Love ‘Carl and the Passions’ to entice Carl into joining.

4gHcu2JoaXJ0mV4aNPCd7N.name: Benny Sings
f: He adopted the stage name Benny Sings in 1999 on joining the Dutch hip hop group Abstract Dialect as bassist.
In 2017 he helped write the Rex Orange County single ‘Loving Is Easy’.
He composed songs for the anime Carole & Tuesday.

3UNrI3SG1l2ezKikxQ2zuk.name: Edgar Winter
f: In late 1972 he formed the Edgar Winter Group with Dan Hartman, Ronnie Montrose and Chuck Ruff.
Early in his career he invented the keyboard body strap, which lets him move around the stage while playing.
As a session musician he played saxophone on Meat Loaf's ‘All Revved Up with No Place to Go’ and Tina Turner's ‘Simply the Best’.

2Tglaf8nvDzwSQnpSrjLHP.name: Cuco
f: He first released music as Heavy Trip before switching to Cuco, a childhood nickname.
His first single, ‘Lo Que Siento’ (2017), has passed 400 million streams on Spotify.
In April 2018 he played alongside saxophonist Kenny G at Coachella.

56UIK6wmbbxuQ6VA20vrWD.name: Lola Marsh
f: The band was conceived at Landau's birthday party in February 2011, when the members began playing songs on an old guitar.
Their cover of ‘Somethin’ Stupid' featured in the Better Call Saul episode of the same name in 2018.
“Echoes” won the Best Song category at the 2020 Berlin Music Video Awards.

6CWTBjOJK75cTE8Xv8u1kj.name: Feist
f: In 1991, aged 15, she founded and fronted a Calgary punk band called Placebo.
At 12 she was one of 1,000 dancers in the Calgary Winter Olympics opening ceremony, which she cites as inspiration for the ‘1234’ video.
In Broken Social Scene she sang on many tracks after de facto bandleader Kevin Drew forbade her to play guitar.

4GO3ufZJ7YsEnQ3PiML2Dg.name: Shirley Ellis
f: Her 1965 single “The Clapping Song” reached no. 8 in the US and no. 6 in the UK, sold over a million copies and earned a gold disc.
All her solo hits were written with Lincoln Chase, her manager, producer and songwriting partner.
By 1954 she had written two songs recorded by the Chords.

2M3vnW1p5w4uPRkLYTbvdB.name: Rusted Root
f: The band formed in Pittsburgh in 1990; its founders included singer and guitarist Michael Glabicki.
Glabicki has cited Peter Gabriel's 1986 album So as an influence on his move into worldbeat.
During the band's hiatus, Glabicki formed the group Uprooted with former Rusted Root members.

0UF7XLthtbSF2Eur7559oV.name: Kavinsky
f: “Nightcall” played over the opening credits of the film Drive and became a major hit soon after.
In the persona's fictional backstory, Kavinsky crashed his Testarossa in 1986 and returned in 2006 as a zombie making electronic music.
He performed “Nightcall” with Phoenix and Angèle at the closing ceremony of the 2024 Paris Olympics.

5GA6j57yIPCBrWk1lTvF9o.name: Lime Garden
f: The members met at a college in Guildford, studied at BIMM Brighton, and dropped their earlier name, LIME.
They have toured with IDLES, Sunflower Bean and Yard Act.
Their second album, Maybe Not Tonight, came out on 10 April 2026.

2K13AVg3bFpHSxDM1vJ0qA.name: CSS
f: The band's name came from a remark reportedly made by Beyoncé that she was “tired of being sexy”.
In early 2006 they signed with Sub Pop to release their international debut album, Cansei de Ser Sexy.
Their song “Music Is My Hot Hot Sex” was used in a worldwide Apple iPod television advert.

1PXStuNqw9YDsim4EhMSq7.name: Dan Carey
f: In 2019 he earned two Mercury Prize nominations, for producing Black Midi's Schlagenheim and Fontaines D.C.'s Dogrel.
He produced and played synthesiser on Wet Leg's self-titled debut album.
He was one half of Danmass, whose only album, Formfreaks, came out on Dust2Dust in 1999.

77mJc3M7ZT5oOVM7gNdXim.name: Her's
f: The pair met at the Liverpool Institute for Performing Arts, where Paul McCartney presented their certificates when they graduated in 2016.
The duo first formed Her's as a joke, filming comedic music videos around Liverpool and posting them on YouTube.
Their debut full-length album, Invitation to Her's, came out on Heist or Hit Records on 24 August 2018.

3WrFJ7ztbogyGnTHbHJFl2.name: The Beatles
f: An early name, “Beatals”, was proposed as a tribute to Buddy Holly and the Crickets.
Harrison played the lead guitar part of “Raunchy” on the upper deck of a Liverpool bus, and they enlisted him as lead guitarist.
They hold the records for most Billboard Hot 100 number-one singles (20) and most Billboard 200 number-one albums (19).

5fmvGUlMVgmnCn45f1he7d.name: Andrew Gold
f: He played most of the instruments on “You're No Good”, Linda Ronstadt's only Billboard Hot 100 number one.
A version of “Thank You for Being a Friend” sung by Cindy Fee became the opening theme of The Golden Girls in 1985.
In the 1980s he was one half of the duo Wax with 10cc's Graham Gouldman.

5fbhwqYYh4YwUoEs582mq5.name: The Spinners
f: The group began in Detroit in 1954 as the Domingoes, formed by Billy Henderson, Henry Fambrough, Pervis Jackson, C. P. Spencer and James Edwards.
During lean years Motown used them as road managers, chaperones and chauffeurs for other acts, and even as shipping clerks.
In the UK they were billed as the Motown Spinners and later the Detroit Spinners to avoid confusion with a British folk group.

4Xn6fPXDrarY8LxXWqlE2M.name: Elkie Brooks
f: After a spell in the short-lived blues-rock band Dada, she formed Vinegar Joe with Robert Palmer.
In the mid-1960s she was a support act at the Beatles' Christmas show in London.
Her 1981 album Pearls charted for 79 weeks and reached No. 2 in the UK, the biggest commercial success of her career.
